name: Eight hours target / 'sleep is looksmaxxing'

lead: 'Sleep is looksmaxxing' is a community slogan that puts regular sleep first among appearance habits, usually with a target of about eight hours a night. People treat it as the base for clearer skin, better recovery and a leaner, more muscular physique.

Proponents say adequate sleep avoids visible signs such as eye bags, puffiness and weight gain, which are associated with sleep deprivation. Public guidance varies: the US National Sleep Foundation recommends about 7 hours for adults, with other cited ranges of 7 to 9 hours for ages 18 to 64.

paras: People set a consistent bedtime and wake time, aim for seven to nine hours, and keep the bedroom dark and cool. It is usually combined with training and diet. Visible changes around the eyes can appear within days; skin and body composition changes build over weeks.
Habitual short sleep is associated with chronic health conditions. No risks of sleeping adequately are described in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: The slogan treats seven to nine hours of regular sleep as the foundation for skin, recovery and body composition. Sleep loss has documented visible effects on the face, including eye bags and puffiness.

lead: 'Sleep is looksmaxxing' is the view in appearance communities that a full night's sleep is the most basic way to look better, usually with a target of about eight hours. Proponents tie it to visible results: less under-eye puffiness and eye bags, a fresher face, and easier weight and body-composition control [1][2].

Wikipedia lists periorbital puffiness (eye bags) among effects of sleep deprivation, along with higher ghrelin, lower leptin, raised cortisol, lower growth hormone and weight gain, which together are the pathway by which short sleep is linked to appetite, cravings and body composition [1][2]. Because training recovery and growth hormone release are tied to sleep, lifters also treat it as part of building a better physique.

Recommended durations vary by source. The US National Sleep Foundation recommends about 7 hours for adults, and cited guidance gives 7 to 9 hours for ages 18 to 64 [1]. Eight hours sits in the middle of that range, which is why it is the common community target.
infobox: 7 hours (National Sleep Foundation); 7 to 9 hours for ages 18 to 64 [1]

paras: The National Sleep Foundation recommends about 7 hours per night for adults, and cited guidance gives 7 to 9 hours for ages 18 to 64; children and teenagers are given 8 to 16 hours depending on age. Adults sleeping under seven hours are more likely to have chronic conditions, and a UK Biobank study reported about a 20% higher risk of myocardial infarction over seven years in adults sleeping under 6 hours [1].
Wikipedia lists periorbital puffiness, commonly called bags under the eyes, among the effects of sleep deprivation [1].

Sleep deprivation has been associated with higher ghrelin (a hunger hormone) and lower leptin (a fullness hormone), greater appetite and cravings for high-calorie food, and weight gain [1][2]. Taheri and colleagues reported in 2004 that shorter sleep went with lower leptin, higher ghrelin and a higher BMI, and Spiegel and colleagues reported in 1999 that cutting sleep from eight hours to four altered glucose tolerance and raised cortisol [2]. Sleep loss is also linked to lower growth hormone and higher cortisol [1].

Experimental and observational work exists on sleep duration and appetite hormones, weight and health outcomes, as cited above [1][2]. No studies on the specific 'eight hours' target as an appearance intervention were located. Wikipedia's coverage of facial or skin changes from sleep loss is limited to eye-area puffiness [1].

timeline.event: Spiegel and colleagues report altered glucose tolerance and endocrine function after sleep restriction from eight hours to four [2].
